articles.title: Oman to Boost Oil Storage
articles.description: Oman plans to more than double oil storage capacity at a port outside the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Perenco Signs Preliminary Agreement to Electrify Production offshore Brazil
articles.description: Perenco signed a letter of intent with Porto do Acu for what it says is the first offshore platform electrification project in Brazil's Campos Basin.

articles.title: Uniper Agrees Major SAF Offtake with Arcadia
articles.description: Uniper agreed to buy 40,000 metric tons of electro-sustainable aviation fuel from Arcadia eFuels' Project Endor in Denmark.

articles.title: Texas Oil Regulator Urges Operators to Report Theft
articles.description: Texas Railroad Commissioner Wayne Christian has urged oilfield operators to report theft, a statement posted on the Texas Railroad Commission's (RRC) website recently highlighted.

articles.title: SOCAR Expands International Partnerships
articles.description: The State Oil Company of the Azerbaijani Republic signed several collaboration agreements with international companies including ExxonMobil at the Azerbaijan International Investment Forum.

articles.title: Oil Risk Premium Is Becoming Structural
articles.description: Standard Chartered Bank Energy Research Head Emily Ashford outlined that there will be no return to normal for the oil market.

articles.title: Oil prices climb for second day over Middle East supply concerns
articles.description: Oil prices rose for a second consecutive session on Tuesday, 29 September, as ongoing concerns over potential supply disruptions in the Middle East linked to the US-Israeli conflict with Iran continued to outweigh indications of improving crude exports from the area.

articles.title: Comstock and SOCAR formalise $1.6bn Haynesville Shale partnership
articles.description: Comstock Resources and the State Oil Company of the Azerbaijan Republic (SOCAR) have signed a framework agreement advancing the latter’s investment of $1.65bn in the US-based firm’s Haynesville Shale assets.

articles.title: Court Pauses $16B Dangote Refinery Project in Kenya
articles.description: A Kenyan court ordered construction to be paused on Aliko Dangote's $16 billion oil refinery in the East African nation, after a group of petitioners filed a case opposing the project.

articles.title: The Hidden Tradeoffs of a U.S. Diesel Export Ban
articles.description: With diesel prices at record highs, restricting U.S. diesel exports has an obvious appeal. Keep more American-made diesel at home, increase domestic supply, and take some pressure off farmers, truckers, construction companies, and ultimately consumers. President Donald Trump endorsed the idea this week, saying, “I’ve said let’s not send out the diesel.” The administration is now examining possible restrictions as farm-state lawmakers respond to soaring fuel costs. The United States is the world’s largest diesel exporter,…

articles.title: LNG Canada to Double Export Capacity After Shell Approves Phase 2
articles.description: Canada’s first liquefied natural gas export facility, LNG Canada, will double its capacity in the early 2030s after the Shell-led project announced on Tuesday the final investment decision to proceed with Phase 2 of the plant in Kitimat, British Columbia. LNG Canada in Kitimat, B.C., launched exports in the summer of 2025, after years of development by its shareholders Shell, Petronas, PetroChina, Mitsubishi, and Korea Gas Corporation (Kogas). Phase 2 of the first Canadian LNG export facility is planned to add two LNG processing units, or…

articles.title: UAE's Next $25 Billion Bet On India Includes Energy Sector
articles.description: The United Arab Emirates has expressed intent to invest another $25 billion in India, including in the energy sector, Indian Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said at a high-level meeting in Mumbai. The UAE has already invested about $25 billion in India and has signaled its intent to invest another $25 billion in the near term, the Indian minister said at the 14th Meeting of the India-UAE High Level Joint Task Force on Investments. The UAE ultimately targets to have $100 billion invested in India in the long term, according to the minister.…

articles.title: FTAI unit to acquire USDG crude oil logistics assets for $255m
articles.description: FTAI Energy Partners (Jefferson Energy), a subsidiary of Nasdaq-listed FTAI Infrastructure, has agreed through one of its subsidiaries to acquire a portfolio of crude oil logistics assets from a subsidiary of USD Group (USDG) for approximately $255m in cash.

articles.title: India Looks to Boost Exploration as Hormuz Crisis Threatens Supply
articles.description: India needs to boost domestic oil and gas exploration to enhance its energy security amid supply disruptions that drive energy prices higher, according to a senior official at state-owned exploration and production company Oil India Limited (OIL). “Disruptions to global supply chains and major energy corridors can have an immediate impact on energy flows, prices and economies worldwide,” IOL’s Director of Finance, Abhijit Majumder, said at an energy industry event in India, as carried by local media. The Strait of Hormuz crisis…

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Restarts Red Sea Crude Oil Loadings
articles.description: Saudi Arabia has restarted crude oil loadings at the Yanbu port on the Red Sea after the East-West pipeline resumed partial service, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing vessel-tracking data and trade sources. Saudi Arabia shut down the East-West onshore pipeline for two weeks following drone attacks that damaged pumping stations on September 10. The pipeline that helps the Kingdom bypass the Strait of Hormuz resumed partial service last Thursday, but full resumption of flows of about 4 million barrels per day (bpd) would likely take weeks. articles.title: India Unlikely to Ditch Russian Oil Despite Trump's 100% Tariff Threat
articles.description: India cannot and likely will not replace all the Russian crude oil it is importing despite the threat of 100% tariffs on its products in the United States, according to analysts. Earlier this month, U.S. President Donald Trump signed into law the “Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026,” which authorizes and expands statutory sanctions, tariffs, and prohibitions on Russia and extends existing sanctions on Iran. The law allows the President to potentially impose trade tariffs of up to 100% on countries…

articles.title: Argentina Threatens UK with Court Action Over Falklands Oil Drilling
articles.description: Argentina will sue the UK unless it suspends an oil drilling project off the coast of the Falkland Islands, the BBC has reported, citing an X post by Argentine president Javier Milei. "I instructed the Foreign Ministry and our legal teams to initiate international arbitration against the United Kingdom for the illegal plundering of our resources through the Sea Lion Project in the North Malvinas Basin," the Argentine president wrote on the social media platform. "If in 2 weeks the United Kingdom does not halt the illegitimate exploitation, we will…

articles.title: China's LNG Imports Set for Second Straight Monthly Drop
articles.description: China's imports of liquefied natural gas are on course to book their second consecutive monthly decline because of significantly higher prices driven by the war in the Middle East. September LNG flows to China are seen at 5.3 million tons, according to Kpler data cited by Bloomberg today. This would be 8% lower than LNG imports for September 2025, but slightly higher than August flows, which Kpler estimated last month at 5.2 million tons. China is one of the biggest buyers of liquefied natural gas globally but has curbed purchases as prices on…

articles.title: Oil Extends Rally Despite Higher Hormuz Volume Reports
articles.description: Crude oil prices extended a climb that began on Monday, despite reports that oil flows via the Strait of Hormuz have improved considerably since the start of September. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $107.37 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate was trading at $94.31 per barrel. The widening gap between the two has been driven by reports about a possible U.S. ban on diesel fuel exports. Meanwhile, Kpler reported on Monday it had estimated daily oil flows out of Hormuz at 12.8 million barrels, which is a lot more than most…

articles.title: Oil Execs Flocking to VEN Set Off Hunt for Golf Clubs
articles.description: Dozens of executives teed up at the lush Caracas Country Club for a golf tournament Monday.

articles.title: Oil Edges Higher as Supply Tightens
articles.description: Oil rose modestly as traders weighed tight supplies against progress toward reopening Hormuz.

articles.title: Hormuz Rerouting Doubles Cape Traffic Without Delivering a Windfall
articles.description: Over the past seven months, shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dwindled to a trickle, with Iran effectively closing the critical maritime chokepoint ever since the U.S. and Israel launched attacks against it. Consequently, major global shipping companies rerouted their vessels via South Africa’s Cape of Good Hope, with traffic around the southern tip of Africa having doubled since the war erupted in February. articles.title: Why Blocking U.S. Diesel Exports Could Make Fuel More Expensive
articles.description: Talk of a possible ban on U.S. exports of diesel fuel to curb soaring prices at the pump could end up pushing all fuel prices higher, cutting refinery runs as storage fills up, analysts have warned. The move could result in a glut of the fuel in the United States while the rest of the world struggles to secure supply. Retail diesel prices in the U.S. hit an all-time high of over $6.50 per gallon last week amid the global crunch that led to higher exports of the fuel, notably to Europe. articles.title: Standard Chartered: Record CTA Long Bets Are Capping Oil's Upside
articles.description: Oil prices rebounded from their recent slide on fears of U.S.-Iran escalation after attempts at diplomacy yielded mixed results, with speeches by leaders on both sides laced with threats and belligerence. Brent crude for November delivery was up 1.70% to trade at $106.09 per barrel at 4:30 p.m. ET on Monday, while the corresponding WTI crude contract was up 0.95% to change hands at $93.29 per barrel.
